**For 12 or more cells at once, I'd get a 16-bay charger with independent slots.** The search results didn't include direct buy links or prices for the 16-bay models, so I've linked the review pages that list them.

## 16-bay options

- **Tenergy TN438 16-bay (my pick if you want to monitor cells):** It has an LCD showing each cell's status, and you can mix AA/AAA NiMH/NiCd in any combination. It protects against overcharge, overheating, short circuits and reverse polarity, and has an 8-hour timer. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))
- **BONAI 16-bay (simpler, LED-only):** It takes AA and AAA in any slot, with 250-500 mA per port and 110-240V AC input. Red LED means charging, green means full, and flashing red means a bad cell. It won't charge alkaline or lithium cells. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))
- **POWEROWL 16-bay:** It has 16 independent channels and a four-stage charge (pre-charge, quick, floating, trickle). ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/))

## If 8 bays is enough

**Tenergy TN480U 8-bay** is $23.99 at Tenergy's US store, verified 2026-10-21. It has a per-slot LCD, charges at 500 mA per AA and 250 mA per AAA, and takes USB-C power. It comes with a 12-month warranty and 30-day returns, and the buyer pays return shipping. ([product page](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger))

- [Buy the TN480U at Tenergy](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.
- The box has no power adapter, only a USB-A to Micro-USB cable, so you need a 5V 2A USB charger. On a 1A source, five or more AA cells charge at only 250 mA each.

The EBL 8-bay is another independent-slot option, but the sources give no price. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/))

## Caveats

- Most of this comes from affiliate review sites that summarize specs and don't appear to have tested the chargers hands-on. Check recent buyer reviews before purchasing.
- All of these are NiMH/NiCd only. Don't put alkaline or lithium cells in them.
- With a full 16 cells, expect charging to take several hours at 250-500 mA per slot.
